items.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: one day James Galway came in with two gold flutes. He let me and my brother play his flutes.

ctx.x: It does sound nice, doesn’t it? Boy, that holds up well I would say. Beautiful. In fact, the tune is “But Beautiful.” You know one thing I noticed about your playing is that you seem to really like to switch octaves frequently.

You know I don’t think I focused on that other than just naturally. I didn’t focus on the fact that I’m switching octaves. Also I guess a sad story I guess in that I’m still involved with it, is someone cut the head off that flute, it’s like a French flute, like cut off the head joint, and so it’s never been the same but there was supposed to be a good repairman and he didn’t ask me about doing it, and I didn’t know you could fit other heads in it, but I sold the flute and had some other flutes. You know you get…

fact I heard it was stolen later on, I don’t know if he got them back or they sold his instruments, but what I mean a good instrument in the hands of a good player helps you play better. And I don’t have the access to the best instruments. But anyhow I like — the sound was so good because I had another instrument, plus my playing.
